result:
I've written and committed the permute design as `696df95d296` on the run branch. It contains `ttnn/ttnn/operations/permute/op_design.md`, the separate `l1_ledger.md` the planner process requires, and the module-device `conftest.py`, which was missing from the test directory. No code has been built or run against it yet; the only thing I ran was one simulator probe to read the L1 budget (3,963,328 B), grid (8×4) and alignments (16 B L1, 64 B DRAM).

Each call runs one program, chosen only from the layout and the permutation, never from tensor sizes or the grid. Each design moves every input and output byte across DRAM exactly once, and all of them spread work over the full grid from the first phase.

| Design | When it is used | How it works |
|---|---|---|
| Page copy | Row-major with the last dimension staying last; tile layout with H and W staying put (this includes the identity, which returns a copy) | Every output page is exactly one input page. One reader and one writer copy whole pages; no compute kernel. |
| Tile transpose | Tile layout with H and W swapped (two of the three traced tile-layout calls) | One reader, one compute thread transposing each 32×32 tile on the FPU, one writer. |
| Staged gather | Everything else | The tensor is cut into blocks. Six worker threads per core each read a block into their own L1 area, rearrange the elements with ordinary loads and stores, and write the output pages. In tile layout the output padding is written as zeros. |

Things the implementer needs to know:
- **Caches in staged gather.** The data-movement cores have write-back caches. The design requires a cache invalidate after each block's reads land and a flush before each output page is written. Each thread's area starts on a 64-byte boundary so one thread's invalidate can't discard another's data. Getting this wrong gives silently wrong output, not an error.
- **Tile transpose is unproven here.** The FPU transpose has only low-level library tests on Quasar. If it fails on the simulator, staged gather already handles those cases correctly, so the fallback is a one-line change in the regime selector.
- **Size limit for later dtypes.** A tile-layout case that moves two leading dimensions into H and W needs up to 2 MiB of L1 per block in bfloat16. That fits on one thread today but will not fit once float32 is supported, so a finer-grained variant is recorded as deferred.
- **Required tests:**
  - one showing all six staged-gather threads did work (output pre-filled with a sentinel);
  - one per design checking it is the one selected;
  - running the op after another program and before `ttnn.to_layout` in the same device session.

Thread counts and buffer depths are listed as values to measure on a timed backend; this simulator gives no meaningful timings.

The spec seemed consistent and covers every cell, so there is no spec-defect report and no new structural impossibilities. I left `ttnn/ttnn/operations/permute/pipeline_logs/` uncommitted.
